articles.description:
For the past several months I have been working, mostly in the evenings, on an application which collects in one place the various things I would have wanted to have at hand when I first started writing Q#. It is called Copenhagen, it is available at copenhagen.strathweb.com, and it is, in the simplest possible terms, a Q# explorer. It has a playground with an editor and a debugger, a set of guided notebooks, a course of short lessons with exercises that check the learner’s code, and a section in which recent quant-ph papers are reproduced in Q#, at least to the extent that is possible on a laptop or a phone.
Everything runs locally. The Q# compiler and simulator are the official ones from the QDK, compiled to WebAssembly, so there is no server executing the programs, nothing to install and no account to create, and after the first visit the whole application works offline as well.
